defensiveAbilities.name: Dread Gaze
defensiveAbilities.description:
Trigger A creature ends a move action within 30 feet of the ascendant griffon

Effect The ascendant griffon turns its head to stare down the triggering creature, and attempts to Demoralize it. This use of Demoralize has the visual trait rather than the auditory trait, and the griffon does not take a penalty on its check for not sharing a language.

offensiveAbilities.name: Carry Off
offensiveAbilities.description: An ascendant griffon can Fly at full speed with a creature Grabbed in its talons, moving that creature along with it.

offensiveAbilities.name: Disembowel
offensiveAbilities.description:
Requirements The ascendant griffon has a creature Grabbed in its talons

Effect The griffon makes a beak Strike to rip at the flesh of its prey. If the Strike hits, that creature becomes Drained 1 (or increases its drained value by 1, to a maximum of 4).

offensiveAbilities.name: Razor-Edged Flight
offensiveAbilities.description: The ascendant griffon glides violently forward, Flying twice. It makes a wing Strike at any point during the movement against up to two different targets; if either of these attacks is a critical hit, the target also takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage.

offensiveAbilities.name: Terrifying Screech
offensiveAbilities.description:
The ascendant griffon unleashes a fearsome cry that strikes terror into its prey. Each creature within 100 feet must attempt a DC 30 Will Saving Throw save. Regardless of the result, creatures are temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is Frightened 1.

Failure The creature is Frightened 2.

Critical Failure The creature is frightened 2 and Fleeing for 1 round.

offensiveAbilities.name: Improved Grab
offensiveAbilities.description:
See rules...

Requirements The monster's last action was a successful Strike that lists Improved Grab in its damage entry, or the monster has a creature Grabbed or Restrained

Effect If used after a Strike, the monster attempts to Grapple the creature using the body part it attacked with as a free action. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the creature's multiple attack penalty.

The monster can instead spend an action to use Grab and choose one creature it's grabbing or restraining with an appendage that has Grab to automatically extend that condition to the end of the monster's next turn.
